acceptedAnswers.text: The clients wanted more privacy without disconnecting the rooms. We kept the footprint and moved two internal walls. The idea was a clear path from shared life to privacy. Halfway through demolition, we discovered a sealed courtyard behind the kitchen, and that changed the design.
We reopened the courtyard and redirected the kitchen circulation around it. That gave the clients a private outdoor place while keeping a connection between the kitchen and the living spaces.

We had ten months from design through completion. The clients set a fixed budget and wanted to keep the existing footprint. The two internal walls we moved were not load-bearing, and we kept the exterior structure. Those were the limits we worked within.
